newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates close sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates close sharply lower.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed sharply lower on Monday on increased arrivals from the 1996/97 (July-June) crop from farms, brokers said.
They said the rates were likely to open lower on Tuesday owing to higher availability of cotton.

Spinners short of cotton were buying in small quantities as rates slid in the past two days, broker Nasim Usman at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said. "The rates are likely to drop below 2,000 rupees per maund (37.32 kg)."
In the kerb market, the rates fell below 2,000 rupees plus 10 percent sales tax, he said.
